hero.headline: DHS begins deportation flights after TPS protections end
hero.teaser: Federal courts have lifted all remaining limitations on deportations following a Supreme Court decision that ended temporary protected status.
hero.body:
A federal judge this week lifted the final legal barrier preventing immigration officials from deporting individuals who lost temporary protected status. The action follows a Supreme Court decision in June that removed judicial review limitations on the program, clearing the way for enforcement actions.

With no remaining legal roadblocks in place, the Department of Homeland Security has begun deportation flights. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated this week that the agency is actively pursuing individuals who lost TPS protections. "These individuals can either self-deport or we'll arrest you and send you back. It's that simple," Mullin said.

The Trump administration has terminated TPS designations for multiple countries since taking office, leading the Supreme Court to authorize ending protections for Haiti and Syria despite both nations appearing on the State Department's "do not travel" advisory list. Over 300,000 Haitians have lost TPS protections overnight and face deportation unless they have applied for alternative immigration relief such as asylum or a green card.

TPS, enacted by Congress in 1990, protects individuals already in the United States when their home country experiences natural disasters, epidemics, armed conflict, or other extraordinary circumstances making return unsafe. The program provides work permits and has contributed an estimated 262 billion dollars to the U.S. economy since 2001, according to FWD.us. TPS holders have worked in essential industries including construction and healthcare.

Krish O'Mara Vignarajah, president and CEO of Global Refuge, criticized the contradiction between government travel warnings and deportation policies. "In a stunning contradiction, the administration advises Americans against all travel to Haiti and instructs those who go anyway to draft a will and submit DNA samples so their remains can be identified," Vignarajah said. "To then compel hundreds of thousands of Haitians into such dire circumstances is an unconscionable abdication of our moral responsibility."

Harriett Cecilia Joseph, a former TPS holder, expressed the impossible situation facing many Haitians. "It's not that we don't want to go back to Haiti. It's just the situation doesn't allow us to," Joseph said.

Removal orders for Haitians in immigration courts have increased 96 percent between March and June, according to the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. Immigration officials have begun placing ankle monitors on Haitians to track their movements, making apprehension easier.

Thousands of Syrians face similar risks following TPS termination. Additionally, a federal court allowed the government to end employment authorization for active TPS holders from El Salvador, Ukraine, and Sudan, threatening their livelihoods despite ongoing deportation protections.

Josiane Valsaint, a Haitian who held TPS, wrote that immigrants contribute significantly to the American workforce. "We work hard, we pay our taxes, we give back to our communities and we are a big part of the engine that keeps the United States workforce in many essential industries moving. We deserve to stay here, with our families and loved ones," Valsaint said.

cards.headline: U.S. and Canada fail to reach trade agreement as 50 percent tariffs take effect
cards.teaser: Trade negotiations collapsed just before a midnight deadline, triggering new tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian imports.
cards.body:
The United States imposed 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products after trade negotiations failed to reach an agreement before Friday's midnight deadline. The tariffs mark a significant breakdown in relations between the two neighboring countries.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney accused the U.S. of making unfair last-minute changes to the deal. In response, Carney pledged that Canada would match the American tariffs dollar for dollar, setting in motion a trade dispute between the close allies.

cards.headline: Federal government orders water cuts for California, Nevada and Arizona from Colorado River
cards.body:
The federal government finalized mandatory water cuts for California, Nevada and Arizona from the drought-stricken Colorado River. The new restrictions require the three states to reduce their water consumption from the river, which has faced declining levels due to prolonged drought conditions affecting the southwestern United States.

The cuts represent a significant reduction in water allocations for the three states, which rely heavily on the Colorado River for municipal water supplies, agriculture, and power generation. The river serves roughly 40 million people across seven states and Mexico. Arizona, California and Nevada will face the steepest reductions under the federal plan.

Colorado was spared from mandatory cuts under the new rules, which will govern water distribution for the next two years. The decision comes after years of negotiations among the states that depend on the Colorado River basin. Water levels in key reservoirs along the river have dropped substantially in recent decades, forcing federal officials to impose increasingly stringent conservation measures.

The Colorado River basin has experienced more than two decades of drought conditions, with climate patterns reducing snowpack and rainfall that feed the river system. Major reservoirs like Lake Mead and Lake Powell have seen water levels fall to historic lows, threatening both water supply and hydroelectric power generation for millions of residents across the region.

The new federal rules aim to stabilize reservoir levels and ensure the long-term sustainability of the river system. Officials have warned that without significant conservation efforts, the Colorado River could face a collapse that would devastate communities and economies throughout the Southwest. The mandatory cuts are part of a broader effort to manage declining water resources as the region adapts to changing climate conditions and growing population demands.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran not ready to make deal as new sanctions loom
cards.teaser: The president commented on stalled negotiations with Tehran as the U.S. prepares to impose additional economic penalties.
cards.body:
President Trump said Iran is not ready to make the right deal as the United States prepares for a new phase of sanctions against Tehran. His comments came as American officials prepared for tougher economic measures against Iran.

Iran warned of a devastating response to the incoming U.S. sanctions and criticized what it called extraterritorial sovereignty by Washington. U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent is scheduled to hold a press conference to discuss the sanctions measures.

cards.headline: TikTok settles children's privacy case with Justice Department for $400 million
cards.body:
TikTok has agreed to pay $400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Justice Department over allegations that the company violated the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act. The settlement represents one of the largest penalties ever imposed in a children's privacy case.

The lawsuit, filed in 2024, centered on accusations that TikTok and its parent company ByteDance collected vast amounts of data from millions of users under the age of 13. The Justice Department alleged that the platform gathered this personal information without notifying parents or obtaining their consent, as required by federal law.

Under the settlement terms, TikTok will pay the $400 million penalty to resolve the government's claims. The agreement addresses concerns about how the company manages privacy protections for its youngest users and handles their personal data. The size of the penalty reflects the scale of TikTok's user base and the government's emphasis on protecting children's digital privacy.

This settlement comes as TikTok continues to face regulatory scrutiny in the United States. The platform has more than 150 million American users and has become a cultural phenomenon, particularly among teenagers and young adults. The company has repeatedly emphasized its commitment to user safety and privacy protections but has faced persistent questions from lawmakers and regulators about its data security practices.

The $400 million figure places this settlement among the highest financial penalties ever levied in cases involving children's online privacy. Previous major settlements in this area have typically resulted in significantly smaller fines, making this agreement a notable enforcement action by federal authorities.

Meanwhile, regulatory concerns about TikTok's age verification practices have extended beyond the United States. The UK's online regulator, Ofcom, announced it is conducting a formal investigation into whether TikTok has adequately protected children from harmful content. The watchdog expressed particular concern about TikTok's method of inferring children's ages, suggesting the approach may have failed to correctly identify a significant proportion of young users.

Ofcom said compliance failures could result in fines of up to 18 million pounds or 10 percent of qualifying worldwide revenue, whichever is larger. Harmful content includes material about disordered eating, self-harm, suicide and pornography.

TikTok has said it requires users to enter a date of birth when creating an account and uses technology to check for indicators that someone may not meet minimum age requirements. The company stated it strictly enforces age-appropriate experiences and is confident it meets its obligations under the UK's Online Safety Act.

Ofcom's investigation reflects broader global concerns about how social media platforms verify user ages and protect minors from inappropriate content.

cards.headline: Boeing engineers and technicians reject contract offer, authorize potential strike
cards.teaser: Union members at Boeing voted down a contract proposal and approved strike authorization if a new agreement is not reached by October.
cards.body:
Boeing's engineers and technicians voted to reject the company's contract offer and authorized their union to call a strike if negotiations fail to reach an agreement by October.

The rejected proposal means Boeing must return to bargaining discussions with union representatives to address worker concerns. A potential strike could affect the aerospace manufacturer's production at a time when the company is already grappling with operational and regulatory difficulties.

cards.headline: Russian Strike on Ukrainian Shopping Mall Kills 16, Injures 130
cards.teaser: A Russian drone strike on a shopping mall in Ukraine killed at least 16 people and injured 130 others, including children, according to Ukrainian officials.
cards.body:
A Russian drone strike on a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine's president's hometown, killed 16 people and injured 130 others, including children. Nine people remain missing as rescue teams continue searching through the wreckage. President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the attack as "cynical and despicable."

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called the strike "terror by design." She announced plans to propose the harshest Russia sanctions since the war began when EU ministers meet in Ireland next month.

hero.headline: Lebanon Struggles to Control Hezbollah After Israel Conflict
hero.teaser: President Joseph Aoun took office with a mandate to reassert government control over the militant group that dragged Lebanon into war with Israel.
hero.body:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun took office with broad public support for reasserting government control over Hezbollah, the powerful armed organization that operates largely independent of state authority. However, his efforts to limit the militant group's military autonomy have stalled as fighting between Hezbollah and Israel continues to escalate.

The renewed conflict between Israel and Hezbollah erupted on March 2 and has persisted despite a ceasefire that began on April 17. Both sides have maintained near-daily exchanges of fire in the months following the truce. The ongoing violence has intensified calls within Lebanon for the government to constrain Hezbollah's independent military operations, which many blame for dragging the country back into armed conflict with its neighbor.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a major escalation of military operations against Hezbollah. "I have ordered an even greater acceleration of our operations," Netanyahu said in a video statement. "We will intensify our blows, increase our firepower, and we will crush them." Israel accused Hezbollah of breaching the ceasefire and issued evacuation orders for ten villages in southern Lebanon.

In response, Hezbollah claimed responsibility for multiple attacks on Israeli military targets on Monday and Tuesday. The group said it launched at least four drone attacks on Shomera barracks, attacks on two additional barracks, and another strike on a military post in Misgav Am. Hezbollah stated these attacks were carried out "in response to the violation of the ceasefire" by Israel.

The escalating violence has prompted widespread displacement. An Agence France-Presse correspondent observed residents fleeing the southern suburbs of Beirut, a major Hezbollah stronghold. Israeli airstrikes targeted the Bekaa valley in eastern Lebanon and multiple towns in the south, including areas near the ancient city of Tyre.

The humanitarian toll has been severe. According to Lebanese authorities, Israeli strikes since early March have killed more than 3,100 people. The Israeli military reported that one soldier was killed in southern Lebanon, bringing the total number of Israeli soldiers killed since fighting began to 23, with one civilian contractor also dead.

Two far-right Israeli ministers called for expanding the military campaign. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich urged putting "an end to the threat posed by Hezbollah's explosive drones," while National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for a "return to intensive warfare" and "taking control" of further territory.

Aoun's apparent inability to bring Hezbollah under government control suggests the Lebanese government lacks either the political will or practical capacity to challenge the well-armed organization that functions as a state within a state. The group's continued military autonomy and escalating conflict with Israel have undermined the president's central reform agenda.

cards.headline: US and Canada Enter Trade War After Talks Collapse
cards.teaser: The two countries imposed tariffs on each other after last-minute demands ended negotiations in Washington late Friday.
cards.body:
Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed late Friday night, triggering immediate tariff escalation. The U.S. imposed a 50% levy on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports at the midnight deadline. Canada responded by matching the American tariffs dollar for dollar.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the final deal, describing it as unfavorable to Canada. The breakdown came after last-minute demands from one side derailed the agreement. The tariff war marks a significant shift in economic relations between the two longtime trading partners.

cards.teaser: A Russian drone strike on a shopping mall in Ukraine killed at least 16 people and injured 130 others, including children, according to Ukrainian officials.

cards.headline: Trump Envoy Uses Unconventional Diplomacy Tactics
cards.teaser: Diplomat John Coale says his personalized approach, including vodka and informal methods, matches the president's style and gets results.
cards.body:
John Coale, a diplomat appointed by President Trump, has adopted an unconventional approach to US diplomacy that includes drinking vodka with foreign officials and using informal language. Coale says his personalized methods align with the president's style and produce effective results in negotiations.

Critics argue that Coale's approach leads the United States to concede too much to authoritarian leaders. The diplomat's tactics represent a departure from traditional diplomatic protocol, raising questions about whether his informal methods strengthen or weaken America's negotiating position with foreign governments.

cards.headline: Yvette Roudy, France's First Women's Rights Minister, Dies at 97
cards.teaser: Roudy championed state reimbursement for abortions, arguing access was a matter of economic equality as much as women's rights.
cards.body:
Yvette Roudy, who served as France's first minister for women's rights, has died at age 97. She successfully advocated for the French government to reimburse the costs of abortions, framing the policy as essential to both women's rights and economic equality.

Roudy maintained that access to abortion was not solely a matter of personal freedom but also of ensuring that women of all economic backgrounds could access reproductive healthcare. Her work in establishing state reimbursement for abortion procedures helped cement reproductive rights as part of France's social welfare system.

cards.headline: Father Leaves Seven-Year-Old Son Alone on Mount Fuji
cards.teaser: A man reportedly abandoned one of his two sons on the mountain when the child became tired during a family hike.
cards.body:
A father left his seven-year-old son alone on Mount Fuji after the child became too tired to continue hiking, according to reports. The man had brought both of his sons on the climbing trip but chose to leave one behind while continuing with the other child.

Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain and presents significant dangers even to experienced climbers. Leaving a young child unattended on the mountain raises serious safety concerns, as the boy would have been vulnerable to changing weather conditions, altitude effects, and the risk of becoming lost on the trails.

cards.headline: Sydney Marathon Medal Features Wrong Stadium
cards.teaser: The medal depicts Munich's stadium instead of a Sydney venue, an error discovered by observers online after the design was unveiled.
cards.body:
Organizers of the Sydney Marathon revealed a commemorative medal that mistakenly features Munich's stadium on one side. The double-sided medal was meant to celebrate the Sydney race but includes imagery from the German city instead.

Online observers detected the geographical error shortly after the marathon organizers unveiled the medal design. The mistake represents an embarrassing oversight for the event's promotional materials, though the marathon itself is expected to proceed as planned.

cards.teaser: The social media platform agreed to pay one of the largest child privacy settlements in U.S. history.
cards.body:
TikTok will pay $400 million to settle a lawsuit filed by the Department of Justice in 2024 over violations of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA). The company allegedly collected data from millions of users under 13 without notifying parents or obtaining their consent.

The settlement represents one of the largest child privacy settlements secured by federal authorities. The DOJ also alleged that TikTok failed to delete children's accounts as required under privacy protections.

cards.teaser: The president commented on stalled negotiations with Tehran as the U.S. prepares to impose additional economic penalties.

President Trump said Iran is not ready to make the right deal as the United States prepares for a new phase of sanctions against Tehran. His comments came as American officials prepared for tougher economic measures against Iran.

Iran warned of a devastating response to the incoming U.S. sanctions and criticized what it called extraterritorial sovereignty by Washington. U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent is scheduled to hold a press conference to discuss the sanctions measures.

cards.headline: Six-year-old girl dies days after family tragedy off Shoreham coast
cards.teaser: The child became the fourth person to die after her family got into difficulty in the water.
cards.body:
Saja El-Khawas, aged six, has died following a water tragedy off the West Sussex coast near Shoreham. She is the fourth fatality from an incident in which her family encountered difficulties in the sea.

The girl had been receiving medical treatment in the days after the water emergency that claimed the lives of three of her family members.

cards.headline: Rescuers search Ukraine mall wreckage after strike leaves 130 injured
cards.teaser: Nine people remained missing after an attack that President Zelensky condemned.
cards.body:
Rescue teams are working through the rubble of a Ukrainian shopping mall hit in a strike that injured 130 people, including children. Nine individuals remain missing as search and rescue operations continue at the site.

President Volodymyr Zelensky described the attack on the civilian facility as "despicable." Over 100 injured people have required medical treatment, with many suffering serious wounds.

cards.headline: Multiple deaths after police vehicle and car collide during pursuit near Middlesbrough
cards.teaser: Ambulance officials said patients died at the scene of the crash as police watchdog opens investigation.
cards.body:
A collision between a police vehicle and a car during a pursuit near Middlesbrough resulted in multiple deaths. Ambulance officials confirmed that a number of patients died at the scene.

The police watchdog has opened an investigation into the incident, which occurred during an active police operation.

cards.headline: Tesla recalls nearly 3 million vehicles in China over door handle safety risks
cards.teaser: Tesla and eight other automakers are recalling vehicles in China to address door safety issues, marking the country's largest car recall.
cards.body:
Tesla is joining eight other automakers in a major safety recall in China involving nearly 3 million vehicles. The coordinated action addresses door handle issues, particularly focusing on manual door releases that occupants may find difficult to locate and operate, especially following vehicle crashes.

As part of the recall, manufacturers will install warning labels to help identify the manual door release mechanisms. This represents a significant safety initiative across China's automotive market, with all participating companies working to improve door accessibility and safety across their vehicle lineups.

cards.headline: US and Canada continue trade negotiations as Friday deadline approaches
cards.teaser: Canadian and American negotiators are working to finalize a trade agreement before a Friday night deadline.
cards.body:
Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada are racing toward a Friday night deadline. A Canadian negotiator stated that "we have more work to do" to finalize the agreement.

The talks broke down at the last minute, prompting Canada to announce it will match US tariffs "dollar for dollar." A new 50% levy on $20 billion of Canadian imports has entered into force following the breakdown in negotiations.

cards.headline: Economy faces adjustment period after two decades of low interest rates
cards.teaser: The United States is entering a period of rapid readjustment following roughly 20 years of ultralow borrowing costs.
cards.body:
After approximately two decades of ultralow interest rates, the United States economy and financial system are facing a significant period of adjustment. The shift away from the low-cost borrowing environment that characterized much of the 21st century so far could create new challenges for businesses and consumers.

The readjustment affects the world's largest economy and most important financial system. Economists are watching how markets, businesses, and households adapt to an environment where capital carries higher costs than many participants have experienced throughout their professional lives.

cards.headline: Boeing engineers and technicians reject contract offer, authorize potential strike
cards.teaser: Union members at Boeing voted down a contract proposal and approved strike authorization if a new agreement is not reached by October.

Boeing's engineers and technicians voted to reject the company's contract offer and authorized their union to call a strike if negotiations fail to reach an agreement by October.

The rejected proposal means Boeing must return to bargaining discussions with union representatives to address worker concerns. A potential strike could affect the aerospace manufacturer's production at a time when the company is already grappling with operational and regulatory difficulties.

cards.headline: Alfalfa sprouts recalled after salmonella and E. coli outbreak sickens 55 people in 15 states
cards.teaser: Federal health officials linked a food poisoning outbreak to alfalfa sprouts after dozens of people became ill across multiple states.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

A company has recalled alfalfa sprouts after the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported that 55 people across 15 states became sick from salmonella and E. coli infections. The Food and Drug Administration identified the sprouts as the source of the outbreak.

Health officials are investigating the scope of the contamination and urging consumers who purchased the affected sprouts to dispose of them. The outbreak involves both salmonella and E. coli bacteria, which can cause serious gastrointestinal illness requiring medical treatment in some cases.

---

Note: The additional source material provided (about tornadoes in New York/Delaware and Hayden Panettiere) is unrelated to the alfalfa sprout recall story. The partial Fox Business headlines at the end confirm the same story but don't provide additional details beyond what was already in your original card. Therefore, I'm returning your original card text unchanged.

cards.headline: Gen Z prioritizes investment accounts over homeownership for building wealth
cards.teaser: Younger Americans are focusing on retirement accounts and investment apps rather than real estate to accumulate assets.
cards.body:
Generation Z is taking a different approach to wealth building than previous generations, choosing to focus on investment applications and retirement accounts rather than purchasing homes. The shift represents a departure from the traditional American pathway to financial security centered on homeownership.

The trend reflects changing economic realities and priorities among younger workers. Gen Z members are directing their savings toward stocks, bonds, and other financial instruments accessible through digital platforms rather than building equity in residential real estate.

hero.headline: SpaceX completes 100th orbital mission of 2026
hero.body:
SpaceX launched its 100th orbital mission of 2026, marking a new milestone in commercial spaceflight operations. The company deployed 29 Starlink satellites and successfully landed its rocket on a ship at sea. The achievement represents a significant increase in launch cadence for the private aerospace manufacturer.

The milestone comes as SpaceX continues expanding its Starlink satellite internet constellation. As of August 19, the company pushed its Starlink network past 11,000 satellites in orbit. This single network now accounts for roughly two-thirds of all active satellites currently circling Earth.

SpaceX experienced at least one launch delay during recent operations, halting a Starlink launch countdown with just 28 seconds remaining before liftoff. The company routinely performs last-minute countdown holds as part of its safety protocols before clearing rockets for launch.

The rapid expansion of SpaceX's satellite network has drawn attention to the growing concentration of orbital infrastructure under single operators. Elon Musk highlighted the disparity between SpaceX and competitors, noting that Amazon has not yet reached 1,000 satellites in orbit despite its own planned constellation.

The 100 orbital missions milestone demonstrates SpaceX's dominant position in the commercial launch market. The company maintains this pace through reusable rocket technology and frequent launches from facilities in Florida and California. Each successful landing of a rocket booster allows SpaceX to refurbish and refly hardware, reducing costs and enabling higher launch frequencies than traditional expendable rocket systems.

cards.headline: China prepares to launch moon mission targeting lunar ice
cards.teaser: China is set to launch the Chang'e 7 moon probe this weekend to search for water ice in one of the solar system's coldest regions.
cards.body:
China plans to launch its Chang'e 7 mission on Sunday, aiming to investigate the presence of water ice on the lunar surface. The probe will target some of the coldest locations in the solar system as part of an ambitious effort to understand lunar resources.

The mission represents China's most advanced lunar exploration effort to date. Understanding the distribution and composition of lunar ice could provide insights into the moon's history and potentially support future human exploration. The launch comes as multiple nations intensify efforts to explore and potentially utilize lunar resources.

cards.headline: Startup develops AI system to analyze living human skin tissue
cards.teaser: Michael Polansky's AI-driven startup keeps living human skin tissue alive outside the body for weeks to discover new skincare compounds.
cards.body:
Michael Polansky, known publicly as Lady Gaga's partner and former deputy to Sean Parker, has founded an AI-driven startup focused on skincare research. The company maintains living human skin tissue alive outside the body, using artificial intelligence to analyze it and identify new skincare compounds and treatments.

Polansky spent years developing the technology in private before revealing the venture publicly. The approach leverages AI alongside analysis of living tissue to discover potential new ingredients for skincare applications.

cards.headline: Trump to award Congressional Space Medal of Honor to Artemis II crew
cards.teaser: The Artemis II astronauts, who traveled farther from Earth than any humans in history, will receive the nation's top space honor.
cards.body:
President Trump will present the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to NASA's Artemis II crew at Johnson Space Center in Houston. The four astronauts traveled farther from Earth than any humans in history during their mission around the moon.

The Congressional Space Medal of Honor represents the nation's highest recognition for achievements in space exploration. The Artemis II mission marked a significant milestone in NASA's program to return humans to the moon and eventually send astronauts to Mars.

cards.headline: Japanese space startup Letara raises $16 million to expand rocket technology
cards.teaser: Letara secured funding to move its hybrid rocket technology beyond small satellite thrusters into broader space, defense and security markets.
cards.body:
Japanese space startup Letara raised ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) to expand its hybrid rocket technology beyond its current applications. The company is targeting broader markets in space, defense and security sectors.

Letara's hybrid rocket approach combines elements of solid and liquid rocket engines. The funding demonstrates growing investor interest in space technology companies developing advanced propulsion systems for aerospace applications.

cards.headline: Nintendo removes hundreds of Switch emulator repositories from GitHub
cards.teaser: Nintendo wiped out more than 400 Switch emulator repositories in a single day as part of its ongoing enforcement efforts.
cards.body:
Nintendo conducted a sweeping takedown of over 400 Switch emulator repositories on GitHub in a single day. The removed repositories contained code and tools that enabled users to play Nintendo Switch games on unauthorized devices and platforms.

This action reflects Nintendo's ongoing commitment to protecting its intellectual property and controlling how its games are distributed and played. The company has consistently used legal action and technical measures to prevent unauthorized emulation of its gaming systems.

cards.headline: Partial lunar eclipse set for August 27-28
cards.teaser: A partial lunar eclipse will be visible this week, with viewing opportunities across multiple regions.
cards.body:
A partial lunar eclipse will occur on August 27-28, providing viewing opportunities for observers in various locations. The eclipse is being described as a deep partial lunar eclipse, with the moon passing through Earth's shadow.

Visibility will vary by geographic location, with specific viewing windows for regions including central Ohio and Oregon's Willamette Valley. The event is sometimes referred to as a blood moon due to the reddish color the moon can take on during an eclipse.

hero.headline: Klay Thompson joins Heat after Mavericks buyout
hero.body:
Klay Thompson has agreed to join the Miami Heat after reaching a contract buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. The four-time NBA champion will sign a two-year deal with Miami, bringing him together with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the Heat roster.

Thompson's departure from Dallas comes after a turbulent period with the Mavericks. Despite the chaos within the organization, Thompson handled the situation gracefully according to reports. The exact terms of the buyout agreement were not disclosed, but the arrangement clears the way for the veteran guard to pursue a championship with his new team.

The 36-year-old Thompson spent the majority of his career with the Golden State Warriors, where he won four NBA titles alongside Stephen Curry and Draymond Green. He signed with the Mavericks last summer but the relationship proved short-lived. His tenure in Dallas was marked by organizational instability, though Thompson maintained professionalism throughout.

The Heat acquisition reunites Thompson with Antetokounmpo, forming a veteran pairing that adds significant firepower to Miami's roster. Thompson's shooting ability and championship experience make him a valuable addition as the Heat look to contend in the Eastern Conference. The two-year commitment suggests both Thompson and the Heat organization view this as a serious push for another title run.

The move represents the latest shift in what has been a nomadic final chapter of Thompson's career. After 13 seasons in Golden State, his brief stop in Dallas gives way to a new opportunity in South Beach. Miami gains a proven scorer and defender with extensive playoff experience, while Thompson gets a fresh start with a team built around another superstar in Antetokounmpo.

cards.headline: Russell wins Dutch Grand Prix sprint race
cards.teaser: Mercedes driver George Russell led from pole position to victory in the sprint race at the Dutch Grand Prix.
cards.body:
George Russell secured victory in the Dutch Grand Prix sprint race, converting his pole position into a commanding performance from start to finish. The Mercedes driver maintained control throughout, never losing the lead he established at the start.

The win positions Russell strongly ahead of Sunday's main grand prix at Zandvoort. Meanwhile, Gabriel Bortoleto faces investigation for an unsafe release during qualifying, which could impact his points prospects.

cards.headline: Chelsea extends Joao Pedro's contract through 2034
cards.teaser: Chelsea striker Joao Pedro has signed a new long-term contract that keeps him at the club until at least 2032.
cards.body:
Chelsea striker Joao Pedro has signed a new contract extension with the club. The deal keeps him at Stamford Bridge until 2032, with the option to extend for two additional years, potentially taking his stay through 2034.

The contract extension represents Chelsea's commitment to Pedro as a key part of their attacking lineup for years to come.

cards.headline: Bejlek reaches first WTA 1000 semifinal, will face Gauff
cards.teaser: Czech player Sara Bejlek upset Madison Keys to advance to the Cincinnati Open semifinals, where she will meet Coco Gauff.
cards.body:
Czech player Sara Bejlek upset American Madison Keys at the Cincinnati Open to advance to her first WTA 1000 semifinal. The victory represents a significant milestone in Bejlek's career as she continues an impressive run at the tournament.

Bejlek will face fourth seed Coco Gauff in the next round as she looks to continue her stunning performance.

cards.headline: Serrano earns 50th career win in bout streamed on TikTok
cards.teaser: Amanda Serrano secured her 50th professional victory against Lucrecia Manzur in a fight that drew over three million views on TikTok.
cards.body:
Amanda Serrano secured her 50th professional boxing victory against Lucrecia Manzur, a fight that pushed her harder than expected. The bout was streamed on TikTok, where it garnered over 3.4 million views, highlighting the platform's growing role in boxing viewership.

The milestone victory represents another significant achievement in Serrano's decorated career, as she continues to expand her reach beyond traditional boxing audiences through social media.

cards.headline: Messi fined for slapping opponent in MLS match
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi received a fine from Major League Soccer after slapping Philadelphia Union's Quinn during a midweek draw.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi has been fined by Major League Soccer following an incident during Inter Miami's 2-2 draw with Philadelphia Union on Wednesday. The 39-year-old forward slapped Quinn Sullivan of the Union, catching the midfielder around the back of the head.

The altercation occurred after Sullivan appeared to elbow Messi following a play. The referee intervened to prevent the situation from escalating further. The fine marks a rare disciplinary action against the Argentine superstar during his time in MLS.

cards.headline: Steelers quarterbacks struggle in preseason loss to Jets
cards.teaser: Pittsburgh quarterbacks Will Howard and Kyle Allar both faltered in a preseason defeat to the New York Jets.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterbacks put up poor performances in their second preseason game against the New York Jets. Will Howard threw two interceptions in the loss, putting his roster spot in jeopardy according to reports.

Both Howard and Kyle Allar failed to generate offensive momentum for Pittsburgh. The disappointing showing raises questions about the team's quarterback depth heading into the regular season.

hero.headline: Hayden Panettiere Dies, Tributes Pour In From Fellow Actors
hero.body:
Actor Hayden Panettiere has died at age 36, prompting public remembrances from colleagues in the entertainment industry including Rose McGowan and Anna Paquin. The former child star gained worldwide recognition for her roles in the television series Heroes and Nashville, along with appearances in the Scream film franchise.

Panettiere achieved breakthrough fame at 17 when she was cast as Claire Bennet in Heroes, which premiered in 2006. Her character possessed the superhuman ability of rapid cellular regeneration, allowing her to heal from severe injuries within seconds. The show became known as television's "coolest" new program, and Claire emerged as a central figure to the series' narrative. "I love how she's a normal girl," Panettiere said of the character. "I think she's sassy and I think she's a spitfire and she's really smart."

Following Heroes, she appeared in Scream 4 as Kirby Reed, a high school senior and horror film enthusiast who becomes targeted by a serial killer. She later returned to the franchise in Scream VI, released in 2023, playing an FBI agent investigating new murders.

Her other prominent role came in Nashville, where she portrayed Juliette Barnes, an ambitious country singer navigating fame and personal struggles. Panettiere later revealed that she related to her character's battle with addiction and mental health issues. In 2022, she told People magazine that she had spent eight months in rehab. She explained that her troubles began at age 15 when she was given medication to appear energetic during red carpet interviews, saying "things kept getting out of control and, as I got older, the drugs and alcohol became something I almost couldn't live without."

Panettiere had previously discussed experiencing depression following the birth of her daughter in 2014 with Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko. She later gave full custody of her daughter to him after becoming dependent on prescription pills. In her 2026 memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, she wrote about the shame of her addiction and her struggle with life during that period.

Born in Rockland County, New York, Panettiere began her career at just 11 months old in a commercial. She made her acting debut at age four in the daytime soap One Life to Live, later appearing in The Guiding Light. She also voiced a character in the Disney-Pixar film A Bug's Life and appeared in Remember the Titans and Ally McBeal.

Panettiere had begun reviving her career in 2023 after addressing her personal challenges. Her death has prompted reflection within the entertainment community about the pressures faced by child actors and the difficulties many have experienced throughout their careers in the public eye.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Releases Handmaid's Tale-Inspired Song on Limited-Run CDs
cards.teaser: The singer released a new track titled Serena Joy, named after a character from the dystopian novel and television series.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo released a non-album song called Serena Joy on a limited run of physical CDs, with a digital release planned to follow. The track takes its name from a prominent character in The Handmaid's Tale, the dystopian story by Margaret Atwood that has been adapted into a popular television series.

The release comes ahead of Rodrigo's all-female music festival, Daisy Chain Fields, scheduled to take place in Orange County, California the following Saturday. The festival and song release both reflect what observers have described as a feminist focus in Rodrigo's recent public work and artistic output.

cards.headline: Austrian Film Everytime Wins Top Prize at Sarajevo Festival
cards.teaser: Director Sandra Wollner's third feature film took home the Heart of Sarajevo award for best narrative feature.
cards.body:
Sandra Wollner's film Everytime won the best narrative feature award at the Sarajevo Film Festival. The Austrian director's third feature had previously won recognition at the Cannes Film Festival in the Un Certain Regard section before its Sarajevo triumph.

A jury headed by Emily Watson, who has received two Academy Award nominations during her career, selected the film unanimously. The jury described their choice in an official citation. Everytime continued what organizers called a winning streak for Wollner following the film's festival circuit success.

cards.headline: Dolly Parton Shares Health Update, Says She Is Still Healing
cards.teaser: The country music star told fans she is recovering while continuing to work on projects including a planned museum in Nashville.
cards.body:
Dolly Parton provided a health update to fans, saying she is still healing but continuing to work. The singer and songwriter addressed her audience directly with the message about her current condition and ongoing professional activities.

Parton recently announced plans to open a museum dedicated to her career and legacy in Nashville, Tennessee. The museum project is moving forward despite her recovery. Parton, a fixture in country music for decades, has built a career that extends beyond recording into business ventures and philanthropic work.

cards.headline: Meghan of Sussex Reportedly in Talks for Role in The Gentlemen
cards.teaser: The Duchess is reportedly considering returning to acting for the first time in nearly a decade in Guy Ritchie's Netflix series.
cards.body:
The Duchess of Sussex is in discussions to join the cast of Netflix's The Gentlemen for its third season, according to reports. The crime series is created by director Guy Ritchie and serves as a television adaptation of his 2019 film of the same name.

This would mark Meghan's return to acting after stepping back from the industry nearly a decade ago. The third season has not yet received official confirmation for production.

cards.headline: Hunter Biden Appears on Bill Maher's Show
cards.teaser: The president's son continued a series of media appearances with a visit to Maher's program.
cards.body:
Hunter Biden appeared on Bill Maher's show, continuing a run of media appearances that has included podcasts hosted by figures across the political spectrum. Maher addressed Biden's past directly during the interview, referencing leaked personal content that became public in previous years.

Biden's recent media tour has included appearances on programs hosted by Nick Fuentes, Tucker Carlson, and Candace Owens, among others. He has also been active on social media platforms and published writing on Substack. The media blitz follows years of public scrutiny and legal issues that have kept Biden in the news cycle throughout his father's political career.

cards.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns and Jordyn Woods Marry in Malibu Wedding
cards.teaser: The NBA player and model held a wedding ceremony attended by friends and fellow athletes.
cards.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns, who plays for the New York Knicks, married Jordyn Woods in a wedding ceremony held in Malibu, California. The event drew guests from the sports and entertainment worlds and took place during what The New York Times called a summer of NBA weddings.

New York Knicks player Jose Alvarado said teammate Josh Hart was active on the dance floor during the celebration. Musician Jaden Smith created custom size 20 Louboutin shoes for Towns to wear at the wedding. Woods used a depuffing wand for her bridal appearance, according to beauty coverage of the event.

hero.headline: DHS begins deportation flights after TPS protections end
hero.teaser: Federal courts have lifted all remaining limitations on deportations following a Supreme Court decision that ended temporary protected status.
hero.body:
A federal judge this week lifted the final legal barrier preventing immigration officials from deporting individuals who lost temporary protected status. The action follows a Supreme Court decision in June that removed judicial review limitations on the program, clearing the way for enforcement actions.

With no remaining legal roadblocks in place, the Department of Homeland Security has begun deportation flights. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated this week that the agency is actively pursuing individuals who lost TPS protections. "These individuals can either self-deport or we'll arrest you and send you back. It's that simple," Mullin said.

The Trump administration has terminated TPS designations for multiple countries since taking office, leading the Supreme Court to authorize ending protections for Haiti and Syria despite both nations appearing on the State Department's "do not travel" advisory list. Over 300,000 Haitians have lost TPS protections overnight and face deportation unless they have applied for alternative immigration relief such as asylum or a green card.

TPS, enacted by Congress in 1990, protects individuals already in the United States when their home country experiences natural disasters, epidemics, armed conflict, or other extraordinary circumstances making return unsafe. The program provides work permits and has contributed an estimated 262 billion dollars to the U.S. economy since 2001, according to FWD.us. TPS holders have worked in essential industries including construction and healthcare.

Krish O'Mara Vignarajah, president and CEO of Global Refuge, criticized the contradiction between government travel warnings and deportation policies. "In a stunning contradiction, the administration advises Americans against all travel to Haiti and instructs those who go anyway to draft a will and submit DNA samples so their remains can be identified," Vignarajah said. "To then compel hundreds of thousands of Haitians into such dire circumstances is an unconscionable abdication of our moral responsibility."

Harriett Cecilia Joseph, a former TPS holder, expressed the impossible situation facing many Haitians. "It's not that we don't want to go back to Haiti. It's just the situation doesn't allow us to," Joseph said.

Removal orders for Haitians in immigration courts have increased 96 percent between March and June, according to the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. Immigration officials have begun placing ankle monitors on Haitians to track their movements, making apprehension easier.

Thousands of Syrians face similar risks following TPS termination. Additionally, a federal court allowed the government to end employment authorization for active TPS holders from El Salvador, Ukraine, and Sudan, threatening their livelihoods despite ongoing deportation protections.

Josiane Valsaint, a Haitian who held TPS, wrote that immigrants contribute significantly to the American workforce. "We work hard, we pay our taxes, we give back to our communities and we are a big part of the engine that keeps the United States workforce in many essential industries moving. We deserve to stay here, with our families and loved ones," Valsaint said.

cards.headline: U.S. and Canada impose 50% tariffs as trade talks collapse
cards.teaser: Trade negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed late Friday night, with both governments announcing that steep new tariffs will take effect.
cards.body:
Trade negotiations between the U.S. and Canada broke down late Friday, triggering steep new tariffs that took effect at midnight. The U.S. imposed a 50% tariff on approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian products, while Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Canada would match the tariffs dollar for dollar.

President Trump invoked Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to implement the duties. The tariffs affect a range of Canadian goods across multiple sectors, from construction materials to consumer products. Both nations now face economic consequences as American exporters encounter matching barriers in Canadian markets.

cards.headline: Education Department moves to end ABA law school accreditation oversight
cards.teaser: The Department of Education has proposed ending the American Bar Association's authority to oversee law school accreditation after 70 years.
cards.body:
The Department of Education made the suggestion to terminate the American Bar Association's power over the law school accreditation process, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The ABA has held the authority to accredit nearly 200 law schools for the past seven decades.

The proposed change would mark a significant shift in how legal education is regulated in the United States. The department's move targets a longstanding institutional arrangement that has governed legal education standards across the country.

cards.headline: Army Secretary Driscoll plans exit amid tensions with Defense Secretary Hegseth
cards.teaser: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is looking to leave his role at the Pentagon around the end of 2026 following months of disputes with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
cards.body:
A former White House official and another source familiar with the discussions confirmed that Driscoll is seeking to depart his position. A third source said Driscoll has long communicated his intentions regarding the timeline.

The planned departure comes after a months-long turf war between Driscoll and Hegseth at the Pentagon. The tensions between the Army Secretary and Defense Secretary have shaped the dynamics at the Department of Defense in recent months.

cards.headline: Trump rallies for Darline Graham ahead of South Carolina runoff
cards.teaser: President Trump traveled to Myrtle Beach to support Sen. Darline Graham in next week's Republican primary runoff.
cards.body:
The president held a rally in South Carolina on Friday, urging Republicans to turn out for next week's primary runoff election and November's midterm elections. Trump told supporters that the late Sen. Lindsey Graham respected Darline Graham more than any other person he knew, including the president himself.

The trip to Myrtle Beach represents a final push by Trump to boost Graham's candidacy in what he called Trump country. The president's involvement in the race highlights the significance of the South Carolina Senate primary runoff ahead of the midterm elections.

cards.headline: Karoline Leavitt joins Trump super PAC after leaving White House
cards.teaser: The outgoing White House press secretary confirmed she will work at President Trump's MAGA Inc. super PAC.
cards.body:
Karoline Leavitt announced her next position on Friday evening outside Air Force One, revealing she will join President's Trump MAGA Inc. super PAC. The announcement came more than a week after she announced her resignation from her role as White House press secretary.

Leavitt's move marks a return to political organizing work following her time in the administration. The transition takes her from the White House press office to the Trump-affiliated super PAC.

cards.headline: Fake polling firm raises questions about industry credibility
cards.teaser: The discovery that a purported polling firm fabricated recent poll results adds new challenges for an industry working to rebuild public trust.
cards.body:
Median Strategies admitted this week that poll results it released on the Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary and the Los Angeles mayoral race were fabricated. The fake polls have intensified scrutiny on an industry already facing questions about its accuracy and methodology.

The incident highlights concerns about quality control and verification standards within the polling sector. As pollsters work to rebuild public confidence in their work, the revelation of deliberately false data raises serious questions about how the industry monitors and validates its own practices.
